Bhagavad Gita, Chapter 2, Verse 25

“It is called unmanifest, unthinkable, and unchanging. Therefore, knowing it to be such, you should not grieve.”

Unthinkable is a striking admission to place inside a teaching. Krishna concedes the self cannot be captured by thought, yet insists that knowing even this much is enough to dissolve the grief.
